alternatives.name: Render Uploads Group by Default (Always Visible Without Interaction)
alternatives.description: Render the Uploads group as a permanently visible panel/section next to or below the toolbar, instead of only appearing in the dropdown. Similar to how the 'Selected Mixins' panel is always visible on the left side. Users don't need to click the dropdown to see/access uploads.
pros: Uploads are always visible, no hidden state issues
No race conditions or timing issues with dropdown initialization
More discoverable for new users - doesn't rely on dropdown interaction
Natural fit with existing left-side panel layout
Can show recent uploads, upload count, etc. without opening dropdown
Consistent with discovery pattern of other UI panels
cons: Takes up additional screen real estate on left sidebar
Requires redesigning the left panel layout
Duplicates some UI elements (panel + dropdown)
Adds complexity to state management (two places to sync)
May confuse users having Uploads in two places
Deviates from the current grouped dropdown design pattern

alternatives.name: Pre-Expand/Open Combo Dropdown When Uploads Exist on Page Load
alternatives.description: When page loads with query parameters, check if uploads exist in localStorage. If they do, automatically expand/open the toolbar combo dropdown so the Uploads group is visible without requiring user interaction.
pros: Simple fix - just call existing dropdown toggle logic during page init
Consistent with current grouped dropdown design
No changes to UI layout needed
User sees uploads immediately if they exist
Low complexity, minimal code changes
Works with existing state management
cons: Dropdown might close again as user interacts with page
Takes up screen space/covers content on small viewports
User might find auto-opened dropdown intrusive
Doesn't solve the issue if user closes dropdown and wants to see uploads again
Temporary visibility - if user clicks elsewhere, uploads disappear

alternatives.name: Show Uploads Count/Indicator on Toolbar Combo Button
alternatives.description: Add a badge or indicator to the toolbar combo button showing the number of uploaded files. When user opens dropdown, Uploads group is visible. The badge provides a hint that uploads exist and are available in the dropdown.
pros: Non-intrusive - just a small badge on existing button
Draws attention to uploads without opening dropdown
Shows at-a-glance count of available uploads
Minimal code changes needed
Works with current architecture
Clear visual affordance that uploads are available
cons: Uploads still not visible until user opens dropdown
Badge might be ignored by some users
Doesn't show upload list without interaction
Doesn't solve the core visibility issue
Another UI indicator to maintain/localize
Only helps if user looks at button

alternatives.name: Debug: Ensure Uploads Group is Actually Being Injected During Page Load
alternatives.description: Investigate whether the Uploads group is being properly built and injected into the dropdown when the page loads with URL parameters. Could be a timing issue, race condition, or logic error where injectUploadsGroup() is not being called or is being called too early/late in the initialization sequence.
pros: Addresses root cause - if group isn't being injected, no UI change will help
Minimal/no code changes if issue is just a call order problem
Could reveal other initialization issues
Most correct solution if this is a bug rather than design issue
Lowest impact fix if it's just reordering initialization steps
cons: Requires debugging and testing to confirm the issue
May need temporary console logs or monitoring
Could reveal complex state initialization problem
Might require refactoring initialization sequence
Time-consuming investigation without clear next steps

alternatives.name: Add Dedicated 'Upload' Quick-Action Button to Selected Mixins Panel Header
alternatives.description: Add an upload button directly in the 'Selected Mixins' panel header (next to the title). This gives users a quick, visible way to upload files without needing to interact with the combo dropdown. Complements the grouped dropdown approach.
pros: Always visible in the left sidebar, no dropdown needed
Clear, discoverable action in familiar panel area
One-click access to upload functionality
Doesn't require users to know about combo dropdown uploads
Can coexist with grouped dropdown uploads
Minimal code changes - just add button to existing panel
Works regardless of page load parameters
cons: Adds another UI button to already-populated panel
Might feel redundant if users can also upload from dropdown
Panel already has filter controls - more crowding
Users might use both upload paths, creating confusion
Doesn't solve the visibility issue in the dropdown itself

alternatives.name: Ensure Uploads Group is Cached/Rendered in Dropdown HTML (Not Lazy-Loaded)
alternatives.description: Modify the dropdown rendering to ensure the Uploads group is included in the initial HTML rendering, not dynamically injected after page load. This guarantees it's always present and visible without timing issues or race conditions.
pros: Eliminates timing/initialization issues
Uploads visible immediately, no async delays
Simpler mental model - group is always in dropdown
No race conditions with group injection
Uploads stay visible across page interactions
Most robust solution architecturally
cons: Requires refactoring current lazy-load approach
Need to handle dynamic uploads in static HTML structure
May conflict with current group rendering logic
Could add overhead to page load if many uploads
Requires changes to dropdown template/rendering pipeline
More complex implementation than current approach

recommendation.approach: Alternative 4 + Alternative 5 (Combined Approach): Debug Injection Logic + Add Quick-Action Upload Button
recommendation.rationale:
This is a two-part solution that addresses both the immediate UX concern and the underlying issue:

**Part 1: Debug & Fix Injection (Priority: Urgent)**

First, investigate why the Uploads group isn't visible when URL parameters (especially expandedIds) are present. This is likely a timing/initialization issue:

1. Verify that `injectUploadsGroup()` is being called when `loadComboOptionsFromYaml()` executes
2. Check if the group is being injected BEFORE or AFTER the dropdown UI is rendered
3. Look for race conditions where query parameter handling might skip or delay group injection
4. Confirm that `toolbarComboState.groups` array includes the Uploads group after injection
5. Test with and without URL parameters to identify the specific condition

Likely root cause: When URL has `expandedIds` or other query parameters, the initialization sequence might be different, and `injectUploadsGroup()` might not be called or might be called too late in the render cycle.

**Part 2: Add Quick-Action Upload Button (Medium-term UX Improvement)**

While Part 1 solves the root issue, add a complementary upload button to the 'Selected Mixins' panel:

1. Add an upload icon/button to the panel header (next to filter input)
2. Wire to existing `triggerToolbarComboUpload()` function
3. Minimal styling - just add to header controls
4. Provides users with an always-visible upload option regardless of dropdown state

This creates a "belts and suspenders" approach:
- Dropdown Uploads group is the primary discovery location (follows new grouped architecture)
- Panel quick-action button is a fallback for accessibility/convenience

**Implementation Priority:**
1. FIRST: Debug why group injection isn't working with URL parameters (1-2 hours)
2. THEN: Fix the root cause (reorder initialization, add guards, etc.)
3. FINALLY: Add quick-action upload button as enhancement (30 mins)

**Expected Outcome:**
- Uploads group visible in dropdown after both fixes
- Users can upload from dropdown OR from panel button
- No timing/visibility issues with any URL parameter combination
- Robust, maintainable solution that doesn't add UI complexity

notes: The Uploads group injection code exists and works (per 03_code.json completion)
Issue specifically occurs with URL parameters like ?input=...&expandedIds=...
Suggests timing issue in initialization sequence when query parameters are processed
Key function chain: handleInputQueryParam() → loadYamlInput() → loadComboOptionsFromYaml() → injectUploadsGroup()
Need to add debugging/console logs to trace execution order with/without URL parameters
Also check: Does dropdown get rendered before injectUploadsGroup() is called?
Consider: Do URL parameters bypass normal initialization path?
Quick-action button approach is low-risk, low-complexity enhancement that improves UX regardless
